notes.1a: This question was answered well by most candidates. The prostate gland was sometimes confused with the bladder.
notes.1b: Candidates showed an excellent understanding of reproduction with many giving a lot of extra information. The question only required the details of the path not the role of sperm.
notes.1c: (i) Most candidates were aware that the chromosome carries genetic information. A few responses showed uncertainty about the difference between genes and DNA.
notes.1cii: Most candidates recognised that the sex chromosomes could be X or Y, the commonest error was to give the sex chromosomes found in the zygote.
notes.1iii: This question was well-answered and many candidates. Good responses that stated ‘head’ went on to describe how it was adapted rather than just giving the structure.
notes.2a: (i) and (ii) Many candidates gave the correct response.
notes.2aiii: The best responses used the information about chlorophyll provided in the question to arrive at a valid conclusion. Less successful responses did not consider the information given.
notes.2b: Many candidates were able to link the requirement for light to photosynthesis and a few also recognised that in the absence of light the starch would be used up.
notes.2c: (i) This question was answered well with many not only recognising the role of root hair cells but also that osmosis and semi-permeable membranes were involved.
notes.2cii: Many candidates correctly gave a function of water in a plant. One misconception was to relate it to translocation and nutrition.
notes.2iii: An excellent understanding of xylem as a transport tissue was shown.
notes.2iv: Most gave the correct response to this question. The commonest error was to name a structure within the leaf. �PAGE�21
notes.3: The data analysis question was correctly and clearly answered by most candidates.
notes.3a: (i) All candidates gave a correct date.
notes.3aii: Most candidates read the correct value from the graph.
notes.3iii: There were some excellent descriptions of the trend.
notes.3b: Some candidates were able to recognise the genus. Many gave the species name.
notes.3c: Many responses described the prevention of diarrhoea and a healthy diet rather than treatment of diarrhoea.
notes.3d: Most candidates gave a correct response to this question.
notes.4b: Many candidates completed the diagram correctly.
notes.4c: (i) Some candidates gave the correct response. A common error was to describe the response rather than the stimulus.
notes.4cii: A few candidates gave the correct effector.
notes.5a: (i) Many candidates correctly gave K and M as representing respiration. The commonest error was to include L.
notes.5aii: Many candidates correctly gave the correct response. A common misconception was that fossil fuels respire.
notes.5iii: Although candidates made good attempts to answer this question, many answers focused on the endangered species rather than the forest itself.
notes.5c: (i)(ii) Candidates demonstrated an excellent understanding of deforestation.
notes.5d: (i) Most candidates were able to manipulate the data correctly, with only a few minor errors.
notes.5dii: Excellent answers were given by most candidates.
notes.6b: Many excellent responses were seen. The best responses qualified the feature they had identified to show how they were adapted, e.g. having lots of capillaries rather than just stating capillaries.
notes.6c: (i) The best responses qualified their descriptions by making it clear that there was more of less of the substance described.
notes.6cii: Most candidates gave the correct response. A common misconception was that there was no difference between breathing and respiration. �PAGE�22
notes.6d: Candidates were able to give an example of a cell and an organ. The commonest error was to give examples from other parts of the body which did not answer the question.
notes.7b: While most candidates understood the relationship between volume and concentration of urine when water intake increases, the relationship between temperature and exercise was less well known.
notes.7c: (i) Some found it difficult to define growth without using the word grow instead of increase.
notes.7cii: An excellent understanding of the characteristics of living things was shown.
notes.8a: This was a challenging question with only a few responses offering a correct explanation.
notes.8b: Many candidates correctly identified examples of discontinuous variation.
notes.key_messages:
Candidates need to read each question carefully, particularly the information given at the beginning of the
question.
notes.general_comments: There was an improvement in the way data-handling questions were answered.
